state.product: MenteViva, iOS cognitive-exercise app for older adults. Warm, no-fail, big-target design, EN+ES, offline, zero third-party dependencies, solo developer. Copy ceiling: 'fun mental exercise', no medical claims. Home deals 3 games a day chosen on the device by rules (value weight per game x days since last played); easy/medium/hard per game, step at most once per 7 days.
state.player: Primary player: the owner's father, early-stage dementia, plays alone on his own iPad and iPhone. Caregiver and buyer: the adult child.
state.games: Visible on his iPad: Memory Lane (pair matching, his own photos), Name the Herd (pick the items of a category), Quick Eyes (an item flashes, find it among 4), Remember Together (his photos with names, no wrong answer). Color Clash and Number Trail are hidden: they fell flat. Value weights: Memory Lane 1.0, Quick Eyes 0.8, Name the Herd 0.7, Remember Together 0.7.
state.playtest_findings: Recent informal sessions: he likes the app but gets bored. Few games, very repetitive: with 4 visible games and 3 dealt a day he sees the same games daily, and some content repeats. The owner wants more variety and a higher ceiling. Before, he enjoyed newspaper puzzles (sudoku, crosswords, word search), card and table games, and sayings and quiz shows.
state.owner_decisions: Add one game per hobby, each dealing fresh content every session, each with easy/medium/hard, warm misses, no timer, no visible score, targets of 60pt or more. Word search, dominoes and decade trivia were considered and set aside.
state.candidate_games: sudoku: 4x4 (easy 4 blanks, medium 8) and 6x6 (hard 18 blanks), generated on the device with exactly one solution; tap a square then a big number; a number that does not fit gets a gentle 'try another'; a 'show me one' button. up_or_down: golf solitaire with big drawn cards; 4/5/6 piles of 3; tap a card one higher or lower than the open card, turn the deck when stuck; easy wraps King-Ace, lifts playable cards and is always clearable; ends on 'you cleared N cards', never a loss. finish_the_saying: the start of a familiar saying, pick the ending from 3 or 4 big buttons (hard: same-theme endings), full saying read aloud on tap; 60 sayings per language, Spanish refranes and English sayings written separately, no repeat until all are seen.
